cases.title: CF opens the worksheet on CFo at its 0 default
cases.notes: First row of the 'Entering Cash-Flow Data' table. Assumes a cleared worksheet. No 2ND prefix: CF is a primary key.

cases.title: Machine example: enter initial cash flow of -7,000
cases.notes: Outflow, so +/- is pressed on the magnitude BEFORE ENTER. Guidebook marks the display with the 'entered' annotation.

cases.title: Machine example: enter year-1 cash flow of 3,000
cases.notes: DOWN from CFo lands on C01. Positive value = inflow.

cases.title: Machine example: F01 shows its default of 1 with nothing keyed
cases.notes: Key evidence that the Fnn default is 1: no value is keyed into F01, yet it reads 1.00. Establishes the amount/frequency alternating navigation order.

cases.title: Machine example: enter 5,000 for years two through five
cases.notes: DOWN from F01 reaches C02.

cases.title: Machine example: group four equal 5,000 flows via F02 = 4
cases.notes: Four consecutive equal flows occupy one Cnn slot. Frequency is displayed at the current DEC setting, hence 4.00 not 4.

cases.title: Machine example: enter year-6 cash flow of 4,000
cases.notes: Completes the pre-edit stream: CFo=-7000; C01=3000 F01=1; C02=5000 F02=4; C03=4000 F03=1.

cases.title: Machine example: F03 shows its default of 1
cases.notes: Second confirmation of the Fnn default of 1.

cases.title: Machine example: UP from F03 returns to C03
cases.notes: First row of the 'Editing Cash-Flow Data' table. UP reverses the alternating amount/frequency walk. DEL indicator lights here.

cases.title: Machine example: 2ND DEL removes the third cash flow and its frequency
cases.notes: Deleting the last flow shortens the list; the display stays on C03, which is now the vacant slot past the end and reads 0.00 with no 'entered' annotation. The amount AND frequency are removed together (p. 44).

cases.title: Machine example: two UP presses reach C02 from C03
cases.notes: C03 -> F02 -> C02, confirming the vacated C03 still occupies a navigable slot and that UP steps through frequencies.

cases.title: Machine example: 2ND INS inserts 4,000 at C02 and shifts the rest up
cases.notes: The new flow lands AT the selected slot; the old C02 is renumbered to C03. INS indicator confirms availability.

cases.title: Machine example: the inserted C02 gets frequency 1 without keying
cases.notes: F02 was 4 before the insert. The inserted slot takes the Fnn default of 1 and the old F02=4 travels with its amount to F03.

cases.title: Machine example: the displaced 5,000 now sits at C03
cases.notes: Verification row. Confirms insert renumbers upward.

cases.title: Machine example: the displaced frequency 4 travels to F03
cases.notes: DISCREPANCY: the guidebook prints '4.0' here, the only one-decimal display in a table that is otherwise uniformly two-decimal (4,000.00 / 1.00 / 5,000.00) at the DEC=2 default. Treated as a typesetting slip; 4.00 asserted. Proves frequency follows its amount when flows shift. Final edited stream: CFo=-7000; C01=3000 F01=1; C02=4000 F02=1; C03=5000 F03=4.

cases.title: Machine example: NPV key opens the discount rate I at 0
cases.notes: NPV lands on I, not on NPV. I is the Cash Flow worksheet's own rate variable, independent of the TVM worksheet's I/Y.

cases.title: Machine example: enter a 20% per-period discount rate
cases.notes: Entered as a percent, per cash-flow period. Periods are annual here, so the company's 20% annual target rate is used directly.

cases.title: Machine example: compute NPV = 7,266.44 at 20%
cases.notes: ARBITER CASE for the NPV formula. Stream is the EDITED one (C02=4000 F02=1; C03=5000 F03=4), not the originally entered one. Exact value 7266.4394718793. The appendix (p. 76) prints the discount exponent as (1+i)^(-S_j-1); read literally that yields 277.46 and fails. The correct exponent is (1+i)^(-S_{j-1}) with S_0=0. Guidebook states 'NPV is $7,266.44'. If a run of these cases skipped the edit steps the pre-edit stream would give 7,625.99 instead.

cases.title: Machine example: IRR key opens IRR at 0
cases.notes: IRR reads 0.00 despite NPV having just been computed, so computing NPV does not populate IRR.

cases.title: Machine example: compute IRR = 52.71%
cases.notes: ARBITER CASE for IRR. Exact root 52.7053745072%, displayed 52.71 at DEC=2. Guidebook states 'IRR is 52.71%'. Result is in percent, not a decimal. One sign change (CFo negative, all Cnn positive) so exactly one root exists. No discount rate is consumed: I=20 is ignored by IRR. Requires no more than ~13 significant digits of root-finding accuracy to round correctly.

cases.title: Lease example: reset all variables to defaults
cases.notes: Displays the RST acknowledgement. Resets every calculator variable and format, Cash Flow worksheet included.

cases.title: Lease example: CFo is 0 after reset and is left at 0
cases.notes: CFo is deliberately left at 0: it represents month 1 of the four-month $0 group. Beginning-of-period timing is modelled structurally by promoting the first payment into CFo, because BGN/END does not affect this worksheet.

cases.title: Lease example: step past C01, leaving it at its 0 default
cases.notes: No value is keyed. Demonstrates that a slot may be skipped and retains its existing value. The guidebook prints an 'entered' annotation on this display, which appears spurious since nothing was keyed.

cases.title: Lease example: first group, three remaining $0 months
cases.notes: Three, not four: month 1 of the four $0 months was consumed by CFo.

cases.title: Lease example: second group, $5000 outflow
cases.notes: DISCREPANCY: p. 49 prints '-5000.00' with no thousands separator, while p. 47 prints '-7,000.00' and '5,000.00' for the same magnitudes and p. 49's own NPV result prints '-138,088.44' WITH a separator. The BA II Plus groups digits unconditionally; the comma-grouped form is asserted. Lease payments are outflows from the lessee, hence +/-, even though the p. 49 time-line diagram draws them unsigned.

cases.title: Lease example: eight months at $5000
cases.notes: Grouping is what fits a 36-month lease into six Cnn slots.

cases.title: Lease example: third group, $0 months
cases.notes: Left at default 0. A $0 group still consumes a Cnn slot because it must occupy time on the line.

cases.title: Lease example: three $0 months
cases.notes: Matches the schedule row '3 months / $0'.

cases.title: Lease example: fourth group, $6000 outflow
cases.notes: Guidebook prints '-6000.00'; comma-grouped form asserted, as for C02. The p. 49 diagram labels this group '$600', off by a factor of ten from the schedule and the keystrokes.

cases.title: Lease example: nine months at $6000
Lease example: fifth group, $0 months
cases.notes: Left at default 0.

cases.title: Lease example: two $0 months
Lease example: sixth group, $7000 outflow
cases.notes: Guidebook prints '-7000.00'; comma-grouped form asserted.

cases.title: Lease example: ten months at $7000
cases.notes: Completes the 36-month line: CFo(1) + 3 + 8 + 3 + 9 + 2 + 10 = 36 months.

cases.title: Lease example: NPV key opens I at 0
cases.notes: The guidebook labels this step 'Select NPV' but the display lands on I.

cases.title: Lease example: convert 10% annual to a monthly rate on the entry line
cases.notes: CRITICAL PRECISION CASE. ENTER completes the pending division and stores the result. The DISPLAY rounds to 0.83 at DEC=2 but the STORED value is 0.8333333333333. An implementation that stores the rounded 0.83 still passes this case but fails the next one by $92.89 (-138,181.32 vs -138,088.44). The worksheet has no P/Y mechanism, so the annual rate must be divided by hand. '/' is the divide key.

cases.title: Lease example: compute NPV = -138,088.44
cases.notes: ARBITER CASE. Exact value -138088.4358224 using the unrounded stored I of 0.8333333333333; verified against the corrected exponent (1+i)^(-S_{j-1}). Negative because every flow is an outflow with no offsetting inflow, so this is a present value of payments rather than a profitability signal. Confirms zero-valued groups (C01, C03, C05) contribute nothing but still advance the period counter S_j. Also confirms BGN/END is inert: beginning-of-period timing came from promoting month 1 into CFo, not from a mode setting.
